title: CLO Tips Workshop - Snap Button Manufacturing Techniques
description: CLO technical experts teach you how to quickly create simple snap buttons using fabric pieces and accessories, adding flair to your designs!
transcript:
First of all, add the plate buckle as a custom button.  
Select the button in the object window, then find the plus sign next to the shape. Click the plus sign to enter the custom button interface.  
First, rename it to "plate buckle," then open the button OBJ and select the grid.  
Set the corresponding width and thickness according to the ratio. The axis conversion has already been pre-adjusted here, so no specific settings are needed.  
We also made a video explaining the custom button, which you can watch step by step.  
Next, let's create a pattern for the buckle head side.  
Make a width of 45 mm and a height of 1 mm, select this plate, and use the other half of the inner column from the column layer.  
Combine the particles of these two plates.  
Change the width of the column to 5, the collision thickness to 1, and the curve thickness to 2.  
Then place the plate buckle in the 3D window, freeze the top plate, and simulate the bottom plate naturally.  
After the simulation is complete, freeze the entire object.  
Copy the plate on the other side.  
Use the edit tool to select the leftmost side and pull it to the left.  
While pulling, right-click to edit the movement distance.  
Enter 10 mm.  
We can use a fixed pin.  
Select the front end at the back of the plate, and select the position where the key-shaped ring is located.  
It is recommended to add two fixed pins separately on the ring.  
Next, move the sewing line to about the halfway point.  
Select the plate.  
First, remove the frozen hole.  
Then use the positioning ball to pull along the X-axis toward the middle, creating a reunion part in the center.  
Then move it toward us.  
After completing this operation, simulate.  
Pull two fixed pins and add a round plate with a diameter of 15 mm.  
Change the particle diameter of the plate to 5, and the collision thickness to 1.  
Add a sticky layer to it.  
The type of bottom ring chosen cannot be stretched.  
Adjust its position close to the ring.  
Then use the free sewing tool to sew the plate and the round plate together.  
At this time, you can switch to the texture surface for better clarity according to the 3D window.  
Use sensitive sewing.  
After sewing, simulate.  
Then delete the fixed pins.  
Simulate again to make it look more natural.  
Here you can see there is a slight unnaturalness at the opening.  
We can set the folding angle here to 270 degrees to make it perpendicular to the round plate.  
This area is a bit unstable.  
We can turn off folding at this spot in the attribute editor.  
If it still doesn't work, turn it off.  
If instability persists, delete the sewing line, recheck stability, and sew again.  
At this point, you can see it is relatively stable.  
Then switch to the back view.  
Use a fake sewing needle to fix the round plate and the other side of the plate.  
Perform the sewing.  
When fixing, pay attention to the fixing position.  
Because the plate is facing us, the fixed position should be at the edge of the plate, not near the center.  
Adjust the position of the fake sewing needle.  
Combine the angle to determine its position.  
After adjustment, delete the fixed pins on the ring part.  
Combine the simulation effect.  
Adjust the position of the fixed pin at the end of the hinge.  
Next, add the buckle of the plate buckle to the round plate.  
Select the buckle.  
In the property editor, turn off conflict.  
Adjust the size of the round plate.  
Here, double-click the center point after selecting the round plate.  
When the top of the outer frame turns orange, you can use the center point as a reference to quickly adjust the plate size.  
Finally, adjust the stitching of the buckle to make the plate buckle look more natural.  
Next, apply transparent fabric to this round plate.  
Select the round plate.  
Apply a new default fabric.  
Reduce the opacity to the lowest level.  
At this time, the round plate is transparent.  
Delete all fixed pins.  
Remove the frozen hole on the other side of the buckle.  
Save it as a clothing document for convenient use next time.  
Next, add the plate buckle to our clothing.  
Click to add clothing.  
Add the plate buckle document.  
Click to add clothing.  
Click to add clothing again.  
Then, in the 2D window,  
Place the plate buckle on the blank.  
In the 3D window,  
Add the buckle near the desired location.  
The demonstration here is:  
The left side facing us is a buckle,  
The right side is a buckle.  
You can see that the sewing position has been pre-set.  
The internal line here will be slightly longer than the buckle,  
The extra length facilitates adjustment.  
Adjust the buckles on both sides to straighten them.  
You can add one more.  
After tightening one internal line,  
Set another internal line as needed.  
As a reference,  
Here are two internal lines with a diameter of 2 mm.  
Next, place the plate buckle on the sewing line.  
Before sewing,  
Change the clothing rendering type to texture surface.  
Use the free sewing tool.  
When sewing,  
Follow the high blue dots in the 3D window to identify sewing positions.  
First, set the starting point.  
Click to set the end point.  
You can set the sewing line length in the window.  
On the left side, set the sewing line length to 25 mm,  
Set 28 mm on the right side.  
Switch to the edge sewing line tool.  
Then switch the view to the bottom,  
Convenient for adjusting the sewing line.  
Keep the seam allowance and neckline seam allowance even,  
Which prevents pulling at corresponding positions.  
After adjustment, simulate.  
Here you can see the seam allowance has some hammering effect.  
You can add stitching to the seam allowance.  
Here, choose the hardest bottom collar with no seam allowance.  
At this time, the seam allowance on the buckle side is slightly unbalanced.  
Make adjustments.  
After adjustment,  
Copy another plate buckle,  
Perform the same operation, and sew it to the opening position.  
Next, apply fabric to the seam allowance board.  
Here, directly select the lining window.  
Apply the seam allowance fabric.  
Then modify the material type to make it shinier.  
Change to a uniform color.  
Use the color stripper to absorb the color of the body directly.  
Apply.  
Here you can add color from the color stripper to the color board.  
Here we can copy the PBR sticker of the seam allowance fabric,  
Lock the path.  
Next, apply the PBR sticker to the OBJ app for fastening,  
And modify the material.  
This can be pasted on the previous path in the next step,  
And apply the corresponding PBR sticker directly to the same path.  
You can see that the plate buckle made of real silk fabric has a certain glossiness.  
Then the effect of this plate buckle is complete.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Snap Button Manufacturing Techniques
chunks.content: ## Adding and Customizing the Plate Buckle Button This section explains how to add a plate buckle as a custom button in the design software, including renaming, setting dimensions, and preparing the button object for simulation. - Select the button in the object window. - Click the plus sign next to the shape to enter the custom button interface. - Rename the button to "plate buckle." - Open the button OBJ and select the grid. - Set the width and thickness according to the required ratio; axis conversion is pre-adjusted, so no extra settings are needed. - A detailed tutorial video is available on creating custom buttons for additional guidance. ## Creating the Buckle Head Pattern and Simulation Setup This section covers the creation of the buckle head pattern, plate adjustments, and initial simulation setup to ensure realistic behavior. - Create a plate pattern with dimensions: width 45 mm, height 1 mm. - Select the plate and combine it with the other half of the inner column from the column layer. - Adjust parameters: column width to 5 mm, collision thickness to 1 mm, and curve thickness to 2 mm. - Place the plate buckle in the 3D window. - Freeze the top plate and simulate the bottom plate naturally. - After simulation, freeze the entire object. - Copy the plate to the opposite side. - Use the edit tool to select the leftmost edge and pull it 10 mm to the left, confirmed by right-clicking to enter the exact movement distance. ## Adding Fixed Pins and Sewing Line Adjustments This section details the placement of fixed pins and sewing line adjustments to secure the buckle components properly. - Use fixed pins at the back front end of the plate, near the key-shaped ring. - Add two fixed pins separately on the ring for stability. - Move the sewing line to about halfway through the plate. - Remove frozen holes from the plate. - Use the positioning ball to pull along the X-axis toward the center, creating a reunion part in the middle. - Move the plate forward slightly. - Simulate the plate after adjustments. - Pull two fixed pins and add a round plate with a diameter of 15 mm. - Adjust the round plate's particle diameter to 5 mm and collision thickness to 1 mm. - Add a sticky layer to the round plate. - Note: The selected bottom ring type is non-stretchable. - Position the round plate close to the ring. ## Sewing Procedures and Simulation Refinement This section explains how to sew the components, adjust folding angles, and refine simulation stability. - Use the free sewing tool to sew the plate and round plate together. - Switch to texture surface view in the 3D window for better sewing clarity. - Use sensitive sewing mode. - After sewing, simulate the assembly. - Delete fixed pins post-simulation. - Simulate again to improve natural appearance.
chunks.content_description: CLO technical experts teach you how to quickly create simple snap buttons using fabric pieces and accessories, adding flair to your designs!

chunks.content: - Position the round plate close to the ring. ## Sewing Procedures and Simulation Refinement This section explains how to sew the components, adjust folding angles, and refine simulation stability. - Use the free sewing tool to sew the plate and round plate together. - Switch to texture surface view in the 3D window for better sewing clarity. - Use sensitive sewing mode. - After sewing, simulate the assembly. - Delete fixed pins post-simulation. - Simulate again to improve natural appearance. - Address slight unnaturalness at the opening by setting the folding angle to 270 degrees, making it perpendicular to the round plate. - Turn off folding at unstable spots via the attribute editor. - If instability remains, delete the sewing line, check stability, and resew. - Once stable, switch to back view. - Use a fake sewing needle to fix the round plate to the opposite side of the plate. - Position the fake sewing needle carefully at the plate’s edge (not near the center). - Adjust needle position according to the angle. - Delete fixed pins on the ring after adjustment. - Adjust the fixed pin position at the hinge end for better simulation effect. ## Adding and Adjusting the Buckle on the Round Plate This section covers attaching the buckle to the round plate and fine-tuning size and stitching for realism. - Select the buckle object. - In the property editor, turn off conflict detection. - Adjust the round plate size by double-clicking the center point. - When the outer frame top turns orange, use the center point as a reference for quick resizing. - Adjust buckle stitching for a natural appearance. ## Applying Transparent Fabric and Final Preparations This section describes applying transparent fabric to the round plate and final cleanup before saving. - Select the round plate. - Apply a new default fabric. - Reduce opacity to the lowest level to make the round plate transparent. - Delete all fixed pins. - Remove frozen holes on the opposite side of the buckle. - Save the finished buckle setup as a clothing document for future use. ## Integrating the Plate Buckle into Clothing This section explains how to add the plate buckle to clothing patterns and position it correctly. - Add clothing in the software. - Import the plate buckle document. - Add clothing layers as needed. - In the 2D window, place the plate buckle on the garment blank. - In the 3D window, position the buckle near the desired location. - Note: The left side facing the viewer is a buckle; the right side is the buckle plate. - Pre-set sewing positions are slightly longer than the buckle to allow for adjustment. - Align buckles on both sides and add additional buckles if required. - Tighten one internal sewing line, then set another as needed. - Use internal lines of 2 mm diameter as reference.

chunks.content: - In the 3D window, position the buckle near the desired location. - Note: The left side facing the viewer is a buckle; the right side is the buckle plate. - Pre-set sewing positions are slightly longer than the buckle to allow for adjustment. - Align buckles on both sides and add additional buckles if required. - Tighten one internal sewing line, then set another as needed. - Use internal lines of 2 mm diameter as reference. ## Sewing the Buckle to the Garment and Seam Allowance Management This section outlines sewing the buckle to the garment, adjusting seam allowances, and simulating the final look. - Before sewing, set clothing rendering type to texture surface. - Use the free sewing tool following the high blue dots in the 3D window to identify sewing positions. - Set the sewing start point and end point. - Specify sewing line lengths: 25 mm on the left side, 28 mm on the right side. - Switch to the edge sewing line tool. - Change view to bottom for easier sewing line adjustment. - Maintain even seam allowance and neckline seam allowance to prevent pulling. - Simulate the garment; observe seam allowance with slight hammering effect. - Add stitching to seam allowance for reinforcement. - Choose the hardest bottom collar fabric with no seam allowance. - Adjust seam allowance on the buckle side to balance. - Copy and sew additional plate buckles to garment openings as needed. ## Applying Fabric and PBR Materials to Seam Allowance and Fastening Components This section details fabric application and material enhancement for seam allowances and fastening components using PBR (Physically Based Rendering) textures. - Select the lining window. - Apply seam allowance fabric. - Modify material type to increase shininess. - Change to a uniform color. - Use the color stripper tool to absorb the body fabric color directly. - Copy the PBR sticker of the seam allowance fabric and lock the path. - Apply the PBR sticker to the OBJ app for fastening components. - Modify the material accordingly. - Paste the PBR sticker on previous paths in subsequent steps. - The plate buckle made from real silk fabric exhibits a noticeable glossiness. ## Final Outcome The plate buckle assembly demonstrates realistic fabric behavior, stitching, and material properties, including transparency and glossiness, resulting in a natural and stable clothing component optimized for virtual garment creation.
